gap: Process kills and corrupt images do not prove that a running executor survives full auxiliary recovery storage.

fault.filesystem: unique tmpfs inside executor-0 outer node
fault.scope: checkpoint and block-log bind only; existing state and Aeron mounts remain intact
fault.base_due: age the completed temporary base after filling; keep production flags unchanged

oracles: Verify the dedicated source, filesystem type, exact capacity and task device before filling.
Verify the baseline copy through production restore; require real filler ENOSPC.
Require fresh same-process checkpoint and block-log ENOSPC messages and an advancing block-log failure counter.
Require a bounded 60-second transfer plus victim block and transaction progress while its block-log ENOSPC continues, with zero available space before release.
After release, require a new checkpoint above the fault head, then copy its image and log and require production restore to advance above that base.
Release space even on error, restore the exact saved job, verify its original bind, and wait for no live temporary binds before ordinary unmount.
Preserve common receipt, validator, convergence and persisted-state gates.

negative_controls.mutation: Permit block progress without victim transaction progress

limitations: Live kernel fault, same-process runtime recovery and final performance remain pending CI.
This is not active MDBX ENOSPC, block-device EIO, durability or power-loss coverage.
The temporary filesystem can use up to 512 MiB of memory/swap; performance comparisons must use identical fault settings.
style_review: R1-R16 reviewed. Helpers keep lifecycle, mount validation and evidence separate. Reuse the production checkpoint-copy verifier and one bounded RPC transfer helper. No synchronization, dynamic dispatch, stored/wire format, production configuration or hot-path changes. Boundary parsing rejects foreign mounts and unsupported job shapes.
